title: Wright brothers' first flight
description: The Wright Brothers did not solely rely on engine power to lift their flying machines off the ground. Instead, they emphasized the importance of piloting skills. Through over a thousand gliding flights from the top of Kill Devil Hill, the brothers were able to identify the engineering principles that allow for lift and the necessary controls to maintain an aircraft in flight.

title: First clamshell laptop (GRiD Compass)
description: The GRiD Compass was the first clamshell laptop. It weighed 10 pounds but is still considered the first truly portable laptop computer.

title: Gutenberg printing press introduced in Europe
phrase: Gutenberg's printing press being introduced in Europe
description: Around this time Johannes Gutenberg, of the German city of Mainz, introduced the printing press to Europe.

title: Apple II goes on sale
phrase: the Apple II going on sale
description: Steve Wozniak's design, with color graphics and eight expansion slots, turned Apple into a real company. VisiCalc, the first spreadsheet program, gave people a reason to buy one for the office.

title: IBM announces the IBM PC
description: IBM built it from off-the-shelf parts and licensed its operating system from a small company called Microsoft. That made it easy to clone, and the clones are why we still say "PC."

title: Release of the Macintosh
phrase: the release of the original Macintosh
description: Announced by the "1984" Super Bowl ad two days earlier, the Macintosh brought the mouse and a graphical interface to people who couldn't afford Apple's Lisa.

title: Release of Windows 95
description: Microsoft licensed "Start Me Up" by the Rolling Stones to introduce the Start button, and people lined up at midnight to buy an operating system.

title: Apple introduces the iPod
description: "1,000 songs in your pocket." The first iPod had a scroll wheel that actually turned, and at first it only worked with Macs.

title: Release of the iPhone
phrase: the release of the original iPhone
description: No App Store, no 3G, no copy and paste. All Apple offered was a compelling and intuitive user experience.

title: Bitcoin's genesis block
phrase: the mining of Bitcoin's first block
description: Satoshi Nakamoto put a newspaper headline into the very first block: "The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks."

title: ENIAC unveiled
description: The press called it a "Giant Brain." Six women, Kay McNulty, Betty Jennings, Betty Snyder, Marlyn Wescoff, Fran Bilas, and Ruth Lichterman, did most of its programming, but none of the women who programmed it were invited to the dedication or the dinner afterward.

title: First actual case of bug being found
phrase: the first actual computer bug being found
description: Operators traced an error in Harvard's Mark II computer to a moth stuck in a relay and taped it into the log: "First actual case of bug being found." Engineers had called defects bugs since at least the 1870s, but Grace Hopper made the moth famous.

title: Alan Turing proposes the imitation game
phrase: Alan Turing proposing the imitation game
description: "Can machines think?" Turing found the question too vague, so he swapped it for a game: can a machine pass for a person in conversation? We call it the Turing test now.

title: Dartmouth workshop on artificial intelligence
phrase: the Dartmouth workshop on artificial intelligence
description: Widely considered the founding event of AI as a field. The proposal was optimistic: "We think that a significant advance can be made in one or more of these problems if a carefully selected group of scientists work on it together for a summer."

title: Frank Rosenblatt describes the perceptron
description: An artificial neuron that learns from examples. A single layer of them turned out to be too limited, which stalled neural network research for years, until people stacked perceptrons into layers.

title: ELIZA, one of the first chatbots
description: Joseph Weizenbaum's program at MIT played a therapist by turning your words back into questions. He was surprised how readily people treated it as human; his own secretary asked him to leave the room so she and ELIZA could have a real conversation.

title: The Mother of All Demos
description: In 90 minutes, Douglas Engelbart showed a San Francisco audience the mouse, clickable hypertext, and much of the rest of modern personal computing, running live over homemade modems from his lab in Menlo Park.

title: First handheld cell phone call
phrase: the first handheld cell phone call
description: Martin Cooper of Motorola stood on a Manhattan sidewalk with a prototype and called his counterpart at the competition, Bell Labs.

title: First text message
description: Neil Papworth, a test engineer, sent "Merry Christmas" from a computer to his colleague Richard Jarvis's phone over the Vodafone network in the UK.

title: Deep Blue beats Garry Kasparov
description: Kasparov beat IBM's chess computer in 1996, then lost the 1997 rematch 3½–2½. He accused IBM of cheating, alleging that a grandmaster had been behind one of its moves.

title: Y2K
description: Programs that saved space by storing only the last two digits of the year were about to decide it was 1900. The world spent something like $300 billion fixing them, and the problems on the day were generally minor.

title: AlexNet enters the ImageNet challenge
phrase: AlexNet's entry in the ImageNet challenge
description: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton trained a neural network on two Nvidia graphics cards in Krizhevsky's bedroom at his parents' house. It won by more than ten percentage points and kicked off the deep learning boom.

title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
description: DeepMind's AlphaGo won four of five games of Go, and its move 37 in game two stunned professionals. Lee won game four with a "divine move" of his own. He retired in 2019, calling AI "an entity that cannot be defeated."

title: "Attention Is All You Need" published
phrase: the publication of "Attention Is All You Need"
description: Eight researchers at Google introduced the transformer, which became the main architecture of large language models. It's the T in GPT.

title: Release of ChatGPT
description: OpenAI's chatbot gained a million users in five days and 100 million in two months.

title: Claude.ai opens to the public
description: Anthropic first released Claude as a chatbot in March 2023. In July, Claude 2 became the first Anthropic model available to the general public.
